items.note: A prompt is the instruction you give the model, like a question on a worksheet. The clearer the prompt, the easier it is for the model to answer well.

items.clue: Content from the user in a chat (2 words [4,7])

items.clue: Model reply content in a chat (2 words [9,7])

items.clue: Directive telling the model what to do
items.note: An instruction tells the model what to do. It’s like giving a task in plain language so it knows the goal.

items.clue: Supporting information provided to the model
items.note: Context is the extra information that helps the model answer correctly. Think of it as the background story before the question.

items.clue: Maximum tokens the model can attend to (2 words [7,6])
items.note: The context window is how much text the model can keep in mind at once. It’s like the size of the model’s short‑term memory.

items.clue: Smallest text chunk used by the model
items.note: A token is a small chunk of text the model reads and writes. You can think of it as the model’s basic building block.

items.clue: Process of splitting text into tokens

items.clue: Sample from the top K likely tokens (2 words [3,1])

items.note: Top P means the model chooses from tokens that add up to a probability threshold. It is like picking from a flexible shortlist that changes each time.

items.clue: Upper limit for generated tokens (2 words [3,6])

items.clue: Strings that stop further generation (2 words [4,9])

items.clue: Providing examples in the prompt (2 words [3,4])

items.clue: No examples; rely on instruction alone (2 words [4,4])

items.clue: A single example in the prompt (2 words [3,4])

items.clue: Direct the model to use external tools (2 words [4,3])

items.clue: Model learns from examples in prompt (3 words [2,7,8])

items.clue: Declared role for the assistant (2 words [6,4])

items.clue: Declared role for the assistant replies (2 words [9,4])

items.clue: List of rules or tasks to follow

items.clue: Stylistic or safety rules to obey

Criteria are the requirements for success. They’re like the grading rules for the answer.

items.clue: Make the request easy to understand
items.note: Clarity means making the request easy to understand. It’s like using simple, clean handwriting.

items.clue: Keep the prompt brief and focused

Delimiters are markers that separate sections. It’s like using dividers between folders.
Safety means keeping outputs harmless and compliant. It’s like wearing a seatbelt while you drive.

items.clue: Rules to keep responses on policy

items.clue: Testing prompts for safety issues (2 words [3,7])

Policy is the set of rules the model should follow. It’s like a school rulebook for responses.

Factuality is the accuracy of the generated content. It’s like checking facts before you speak.
Citations are references that support claims. They’re like footnotes that show where information came from.
Sources are the documents that back up answers. They’re like the books you used to study.

Parsing means reading structured output reliably. It’s like translating a form into usable data.

items.clue: Directions for exact output format (2 words [6,12])

items.clue: Ask the model to critique itself (2 words [4,8])

Rewrite means asking for a new version with constraints. It’s like rephrasing a sentence to fit a rule.

Classification assigns labels to text. It’s like sorting cards into labeled piles.
Translation converts text to another language. It’s like speaking the same thought in a different tongue.

Evaluation assesses model quality. It’s like a report card for performance.
